prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on your needs (how much help you want, whether you want in‑person service, whether you need help with ACA subsidies/marketplace plans, HSAs, etc.). Rather than naming a single firm, here’s a practical way to find the best health‑insurance broker in Kansas City, MO for a self‑employed person — plus specific next steps I can take for you.

How to pick the best broker for a self‑employed person
- Prefer an independent agent/broker. They can quote multiple carriers (not just one company’s products).  
- Make sure they have experience with individual/ACA marketplace plans and with self‑employment issues (estimating income for premium tax credits, SEP/QSEHRA guidance, HSAs).  
- Confirm they’re licensed in Missouri. (You can verify on the Missouri Dept. of Commerce & Insurance website.)  
- Ask about fees and commissions. Most brokers are paid by carriers for enrollments, but some charge direct fees for extra consulting.  
- Look for good reviews, local referrals, and responsive service (will they help with claims/renewals or only initial enrollment?).  
- Ask whether they provide in‑person meetings, phone/video help, or only online enrollment. For complex situations, in‑person or concierge service can be helpful.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- How many self‑employed/individual clients do you serve? Any local references?  
- Do you represent multiple carriers (independent) or a single carrier? Which ones?  
- Do you help with ACA marketplace enrollments and estimating subsidy/premium tax credit?  
- Do you charge any fees for your services? If so, how much and when?  
- Will you assist with claims and annual plan renewals?  
- Do you help set up HSAs, QSEHRA or other employer benefit options for a one‑person business?

Places to search for brokers in Kansas City
- NAHU “Find an Agent” directory (National Association of Health Underwriters)  
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup  
- Healthcare.gov list of agents/brokers for the federal marketplace (Missouri uses the federal exchange)  
- Local Google/Yelp/BBB reviews for “health insurance agent Kansas City MO”

Other options to consider
- Online marketplaces (HealthCare.gov, HealthSherpa, eHealth) are quick for comparing plans and subsidy estimates; some also connect you with licensed brokers.  
- If you want a one‑person or gig‑worker–focused service, look for brokers who advertise expertise with freelancers and small business owners.  
- Avoid short‑term plans unless you understand the gaps — for many self‑employed people the ACA plans with subsidies are the best protection.

If you want, I can:
- Look up highly reviewed local independent brokers in Kansas City if you share your ZIP code or whether you prefer in‑person vs remote help.  
- Draft a short email or call script you can use when contacting brokers.

Which would you prefer — a local list (please give a ZIP) or a ready‑to‑use script to contact brokers?
